blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Omnichannel Retail. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Omnichannel retail wins on promise-keeping: availability, delivery promise, price consistency and service resolution across channels. The decision infrastructure behind those promises — demand sensing, allocation, pricing — decides margin before marketing spends a cent.

items: Consent and profiling governance is not yet defined; personalization ships as generic segments.
Forecasts update weekly while baskets shift daily; markdowns and stockouts both inherit the lag.

blocks.x: The pattern composes LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations, AI Proof-of-Concept & Value Validation, Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Demand sensing and pricing, Allocation/replenishment, Order promise and fulfillment) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR/CCPA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
Consent-scoped profiling with clean-room measurement (lift verified)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: streaming signals (sales, weather, local events, search) into daily SKU-location forecasts (forecast error down 20-35%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
